findings.claim: The agent-config check covers only reviewRoot itself, and nothing refuses a review when terminals start in open mode (CommandRouter.swift:948 gives a non-lane worker and the reviewer the daemon's sandboxMode). In open mode the judged agent may write anywhere outside <collie>, so it can plant ~/Library/Application Support/CLAUDE.md, ~/Library/CLAUDE.md or ~/CLAUDE.md, all ancestors of <collie>/collie-review/<x> that Claude Code loads, or ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and settings hooks, and every reviewer then loads them. Strict mode, the default, keeps all of these closed (deny sub(home), agentConfig), so I tried this attack and it fails only there.
findings.fix: Refuse --review, or mute every reviewer, unless the worker and the reviewer both start strict, and check agentConfigs in every ancestor of reviewRoot up to /, not just its parent.

findings.claim: The turn is now measured again after the line counts and the spec read, but it is only compared with 0, not with reviewMinTurn. So a rest just above 20 s, minus up to 200 sequential git show calls, can leave a few seconds: every reviewer goes mute, and that counts as a real refusal (reviewRejects += 1), which is the X3 case coming back through the new measurement.
findings.fix: If the measured turn is under reviewMinTurn, return a marker that runReview maps to .reviewBudgetOut instead of summoning mute reviewers.

findings.claim: On a touched tree, git clean -X deletes every ignored path that appeared during the review, with no copy and no check of who made it. In a paddock loop (not a lane), the Shepherd or the user can work in the same worktree while the review runs (othersWorking is not checked again then), so a .env, a local database or an IDE file they create in that window is lost. discard's patch never holds ignored files.
findings.fix: Remove only the agent-config names (CLAUDE.local.md, .claude/settings.local.json, AGENTS.md, .cursor), or move the fresh ignored paths into patchDir before deleting them, and write which ones in the note.

findings.claim: With --ignored=matching and the default -unormal, a directory that is wholly ignored or untracked and already existed before the review shows as a single '!! dir/' or '?? dir/' entry. A new or edited file inside it (for example .build/… or an ignored .claude/) leaves the status string unchanged, so the recheck cannot see it. This is only defense in depth: the strict reviewer profile cannot write the worktree.
findings.fix: Add --untracked-files=all and --ignored=traditional, or compare git ls-files -o -i --exclude-standard -z with sizes and mtimes, if the recheck has to catch this.

previous.claim: reviewScratch created the reviewer's folder at a predictable path in DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR, which the judged agent writes, so it could plant a CLAUDE.md or a symlink there.
previous.why: The folder now comes from mkdtemp under <daemon root>/collie-review, which every profile denies for read and write (deny sub(collie)), with each component checked by lstat, the parent's owner checked, configs refused and the parent emptied at start. I tried a planted $TMPDIR, a symlinked component, summon --cwd into reviewRoot (its project's parent is <collie>, so no reviewer write branch) and guessing the mkdtemp name (not exposed by list), and none works in strict mode. The open-mode residue is the new minor at WorkLoopReview.swift:60.

previous.claim: 'o revisor mexeu na árvore' counted as a review refusal (reviewRejects += 1) and could defer the task as refused twice.
previous.why: runReview returns .reviewerTouched, which fails the attempt as a move and does not touch reviewRejects, and the failure resets the count in a row; the test reviewerTouchedIsNoRefusal covers it.

previous.claim: A reviewer whose summon failed after its launch was unmarked from loopReviewers while its terminal stayed alive.
previous.why: A throw from launch or ensurePaddock now runs remove(rec) before the defer unmarks it, there is no mark when scratch is nil, and a test (WorkLoopReviewTests ~197) checks there is no terminal and no mark.

previous.claim: The line count ran one uncapped git show per path, ignored truncated, and spent the budget before the reviewers were summoned.
previous.why: reviewLineCounts caps at 200 paths, 1 MiB per file and 8 MiB in all, skips the check past them, refuses truncated output, and the turn is measured after it; the missing check against reviewMinTurn after that measurement is the new minor at :172.
